text:
For most households preparing for a **multi-day outage**, I’d get the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W solar panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit)**. It has a 2,073.6 Wh battery, and the listing says it can cover a fridge and CPAP for about a day and night from a full charge; its 1,000 W solar input also lets you add more panels later. It’s listed at $1,199, though prices can change. ([Kit details and pricing](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-hurricane-season))

A couple of important caveats: the included 200 W panel is a modest recharge setup, and cloudy or stormy weather can limit solar charging. Treat this as backup for essentials—not central air or a whole home. If you mainly need phones, lights, and a few small devices, a smaller, cheaper kit may be enough; the [BLUETTI AC180 + 200 W kit](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit) is listed at $729.

Before buying, check the wattage and daily energy use of the appliances you need to keep running.
